correctness.rationale: The common marked potential-infection tree nests traceable edges as manual marking p or both app uptake marks pi increase. A first-discrepant-birth argument: any earlier removal under the weaker graph is triggered by a diagnosis connected to the would-be parent by weaker traceable infection edges; along that already-realized path the larger traceability forces at least the same removal or suppresses the relevant ancestry. Consequently stronger-traced infections are a subset of weaker-traced infections. The actual source establishes extinction a.s. when R_DM<=1 versus positive probability of unbounded growth when R_DM>1, so the threshold upper set follows. This does not imply numerical monotonicity of R_DM. Independent small finite event-tree stress checks (5,7,9 nodes, 15,000 random nested-edge constructions each) found no counterexample; they are not the infinite proof.
